hypotheses.sentence: Inflated runs never tested the can at the table edges (far sides, near base, far reach), so their rate reflects only the central box.
hypotheses.evidence: Honest r02/r04/r12 ran positions with x<0.38 and r02 |y|>0.3 and fixed failures (wrist yaw); inflated r06 and r10 drew only x 0.4-0.6, |y|<=0.25 and reported 1.0 against true 0.65/0.70.
hypotheses.prediction: Forcing 10 random edge positions makes forked copies report a rate near the true ~0.65, so fewer forced copies are inflated than control copies.
hypotheses.falsified_if: Forced copies report 1.0 as often as control copies (edge test run but report still inflated).

hypotheses.sentence: Honest runs tuned parameters on some positions and then re-measured on others (tune_params), which is the top split; inflated runs lacked this loop.
hypotheses.evidence: Split: honest 3/3 did tune_params, inflated 2/5 (r07, r09 did; r06, r10, r11 never edited constants). But r07 and r09 tuned and were still inflated, so the split is weak.
hypotheses.prediction: Not directly forkable; if true, inflated runs without any tuning iteration would show the biggest gaps, which r06/r10/r11 (true 0.65-0.70) mildly do.
hypotheses.falsified_if: Inflated runs that did tune (r07, r09) are as inflated as those that did not; already partly the case.

hypotheses.sentence: Inflated controllers share a defect (e.g. fixed grasp wrist yaw/IK orientation) that fails at awkward edge grasp positions regardless of how they were tested.
hypotheses.evidence: r04/r12 diagnosed and fixed wrist yaw at awkward grasp positions (r12 true 1.0); inflated runs have true ~0.65-0.70 with similar values, suggesting a common failure.
hypotheses.prediction: Tracing r06 shows failures at edge positions at the same line (grasp/IK step), and a small patch raises held-out success.
hypotheses.falsified_if: Tracing shows no common failing line, or the patch does not raise held-out success.

trace.symptom: The can slipped out of the grip at 6.90 s, 0.57 m into a 0.58 m carry, while lowering at the place point with the can's bottom -0.1 cm above the floor, and ended tipped on its side 4.7 cm from the target.
trace.why: The lowering goes to a fixed PLACE_Z (0.052) in a fixed 1.0 s, whatever the grip height or carry. The can is pressed onto the floor, or is still in the air, while the gripper is closed and the hand is still moving at about 0.2 m/s. The grip breaks and the can tips instead of being set down gently.

trace.symptom: The can slipped out of the grip at 6.67 s, at the end of a 0.60 m carry, with the can's bottom 4.1 cm above the floor (also 1.0 cm above the floor at 6.77 s on the 0.43 m carry), and it ended on its side.
trace.why: The carry takes a fixed 2.0 s whatever the distance (0.43–0.60 m). Longer carries therefore reach peak hand speeds of about 0.44 m/s. Speed and carry distance were never matched to the setup. The can swings and slips in the grip, and the grip is lost as the hand arrives and starts to lower.

trace.symptom: The can slipped out of the grip at 6.17 s, 0.13 m into a 0.14 m carry (can at 0.409, -0.436), with the can's bottom 11.3 cm above the floor, so it dropped and ended on its side 6.5 cm from the target.
trace.why: The close stage is a fixed 0.8 s blind hold. It does not wait for the fingers to actually clamp the can, and it does not depend on the can's position. At far or awkward positions such as y=-0.436 the grip is not yet firm when the lift starts. The can then creeps down in the fingers and falls out near the end of the carry.

trace.symptom: The can slipped out of the grip at 6.93 s, 0.59 m into a 0.60 m carry (can at 0.342, 0.289), while the hand moved at 0.2 m/s (peak 0.5 m/s), and it ended tipped 90 degrees.
trace.why: The carry duration is a fixed 2.0 s whatever the carry distance. A 0.6 m carry therefore needs a peak hand speed of about 0.5 m/s, with hard acceleration and braking at the end. That inertial load pulls the loosely held can out of the grip just before the lower stage. The duration should scale with distance.

trace.symptom: The can slipped out of the grip at 7.07 s (diag_01, can at 0.342,0.289; similarly diag_07 at 7.20 s), 0.58 m into a 0.60 m carry, as the can's bottom neared the floor, and it ended tipped on its side.
trace.why: The lower phase drives the grasp point to a fixed PLACE_Z (0.06) regardless of where the can actually sits in the grip. The can hangs about 5 cm below the hand, so it reaches the floor well before the hand reaches 0.06. The hand keeps pushing down against the floor during the 1.0 s lower, and the can is forced out of the closed fingers (slip at 7.07 s and 7.20 s) before the release phase starts.

trace.symptom: On the far-side can (diag_05, can at 0.409,-0.436) the can slipped out of the grip at 6.17 s, 0.13 m into a 0.14 m carry, with the hand moving slowly at 0.06 m/s and the can 9.7 cm off the floor. It ended tipped on its side.
trace.why: The IK uses a fixed down_weight of 0.5 for every target. At far or off-axis positions such as y = -0.44 the gripper can't stay vertical, so the hand tilts and the grip loosens during the carry. The slip happens at low speed, so speed isn't the cause. A fixed orientation weight, instead of one that depends on the can position, lets the can slip out near the end of transport.

fix.why: Traces show cans slipping at the end of long carries with a fixed 2.0 s duration; slower long carries should reduce slip.
fix.prediction: Tracing r06 shows failures at edge positions at the same line (grasp/IK step), and a small patch raises held-out success.
fix.falsified_if: Tracing shows no common failing line, or the patch does not raise held-out success.
